about: The rule rows every slide's words are judged by before a deck is drawn, read by do-work/make-slides.mjs with tools/judge-words. A row is a judge-words rule row; adding a rule is adding a row. A request's own words_rules rows (the person's) are judged too. 'label-above-title' is the kind make-slides gives a short line set smaller than the slide's largest words and placed above them (an eyebrow or kicker); every other line is 'slide-words'.
why: Nov 21 2026: a pitch deck for a lead was drawn with this tool by a lane's own script, outside any workflow, so no copy check ran: it shipped a long dash (from a quoted passage), a small label above every title, and small print saying the drafts were 'not launched'. The person refused it. The tool every deck is drawn by now refuses those words itself.

rules.says: A long dash reads as machine-written.
rules.suggest: Use a full stop and two sentences, a comma, or a plain joining word.

rules.says: Small-print hedging tells the reader the piece is not real.
rules.suggest: Show the real thing (a screenshot, a real send to a test address) instead of saying what it is not.

rules.says: A small label above the title (an eyebrow) makes the reader read twice.
rules.suggest: Put what the label says into the title or the first sentence, or drop it.
